text:
Tomas: Heads up — we saw two preemptions in eu-west-1 this morning that bumped p99 gen latency from 230ms -> 420ms for a 10m window. Not a full outage but customer-impacting. Looking for a concise runbook for mixed pools: graceful drain + latency-aware reroute + who to paged.

Priya: Ugh, thanks for flagging. We should treat mixed pools as "priority slices": keep a warm slice (5-10% reserved ondemand/dedicated) + a <1min grace window before surfacing p99 alerts so transient churn doesn't flip the autoscaler. Also enable prefix KV warm cache retention for rerouted requests. :thinking_face:

Michael: Agree. For immediate triage: 1) reduce spot drain timeout to 30s so KV flush happens faster. 2) widen routing policy to prefer dedicated when p95>300ms. 3) scale up warm slice by +2 nodes. Example k8s patch we used before:

```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2beta2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-warm-slice
spec:
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 55
```

Michael: And routing override (runtime flag) to prefer dedicated when model.latency.p95 > 300ms: `--routing:fallback=dedicated --routing:latency-threshold=300`

Lia: For pager rules: if eviction_rate > 5/min OR p95 sustained > 350ms for 3 consecutive 1m windows -> page eng-oncall + infra-sre. If it's just single-digit preempts with transient blips, drop to #eng-infra with an incident note. Also add a short playbook entry: who toggles routing, who scales warm slice, who informs support.

ops-bot: ALERT: preemptible-eviction-rate eu-west-1 = 6/min (1m avg). Triggered rule: spot-eviction-threshold.

SRE-Leah: Oncall steps (short):
1) Acknowledge alert and check `eviction-rate` + `model-p95` dashboards.
2) Run quick mitigation: `redwood ctl pools scale warm-slice --region eu-west-1 --delta +2`
3) Flip temporary routing: `redwood ctl routing set --region eu-west-1 --policy latency_fallback:dedicated --duration 12m --reason "spot churn"`
4) If p95 still > 400ms after 6m, increase dedicated capacity (and notify CS).
5) Create incident note and assign follow-up to eng-infra for postmortem.

SRE-Leah: Also, avoid full drain of spot nodes unless they're failing health checks. Prefer soft-drain: allow existing KV cache TTL to expire (30s) and only cordon+evict if pods are stuck >60s.

Priya: Add to runbook: an automated slow-roll policy for warm-slice growth to limit cost shock: +2 nodes immediate, then +1 every 10m if metrics still bad, up to a cap configured per-customer. Also log estimated cost delta in the incident note.

Tomas: Great — can someone add this as a short runnable section in the mixed-capacity playbook? Need the exact CLI snippets and the pager thresholds. I can own follow-up doc if Michael posts the autoscaler + routing examples in the playbook.

Michael: I'll put the HPA yaml + routing CLI into the playbook in the next 20m and add exact thresholds.

Lia: I'll update pager rules and add the escalation owner mapping.

Tomas: Thanks all. Leaving this thread open for the written runbook link once it's in the repo.
